2.3.1.note: 2026-11-23 TD-702: every page-check reader (pdf_pages._open_pdf) is now pdf_layer_guards.GateReader, which refuses a PDF past 4 pypdf whole-file reads and answers a number with no row and no header without a search. Genuine answers unchanged: the gate census over all 870 fixture PDFs (render_refusal, first 30 pages) refused the same 2 before and after, and no fixture makes more than 1 whole-file read. Only crafted files change, and only the three named shapes (missing numbers, wrong generation, comment rows) go from tens of seconds to refused in under 1 s; three more shapes still hold a worker (TD-710).

2.3.2.note: 2026-11-23 TD-710: GateReader (pdf_layer_guards) also caps pypdf's lookup work per reader at LOOKUP_WORK_BASE + LOOKUP_WORK_PER_BYTE x the file size, charged as it happens, including the rows walked as pypdf opens the file (review round 3: rows walked while a broken table was rebuilt on open were free): each file read (call and bytes), each cross-reference row walked, and each read pypdf makes of an object stream's decoded data (call and bytes); an OverBudget pypdf's recovery catches as it opens is raised again. It parses an object stream once (a number it does not hold is a null at once) and refuses an object stream inside an object stream. Not charged: filter decoding, and two open-time scans read through uncounted copies (a cross-reference stream's entries; the object-stream indexes a rebuilt table scans). Review round 4: the second held a reader about 70 s on a 68 KB file and was accepted (already so before TD-710); owner decision 24 Nov: its own follow-up item, fixed next. Cap raised 3x by owner decision 23 Nov (6e9 + 300 per byte; weights unchanged), so a crafted file holds a reader about 3x longer before refusal. Fixture census: same 2 refused, every output hash identical, max genuine 2.8 % of cap. Genuine-shaped files with about 3,500-6,000 packed objects or more, by shape, may be refused (fixture max 792).

2.3.3.note: 2026-11-24 TD-710 gap 2: the two open-time scans pypdf read through its own uncounted BytesIO copies (a cross-reference stream's entries, _reader.py:1430; the object-stream indexes a rebuilt table scans, :1583) are now metered like object-stream parse reads (call and bytes), charged to the reader opening the file; pypdf used outside a GateReader still gets a plain BytesIO. A 68 KB file with one object stream whose index decodes to 70 MB, behind a broken table, held a reader 69.8 s and was ACCEPTED; now refused in about 1.3 s. 2M cross-reference stream entries in an 8 KB file: 9.7 s to open, then refused; now refused in about 1.5 s. 2.3.4.note: OCR-12 new design (2026-11-24): every object number the PDF gate (GateReader) looks up must resolve to ONE object (pdf_object_identity). One raw scan, independent of /Length, strings and comments, finds every 'N G obj' header and every 'obj' word pdfium could read as a header; each named object stream's index is read. A second copy of a used number (another section, an incremental update, inside and outside an object stream, another generation), a header pdfium may read differently ('3.', '+3', '03', a 256-byte number, a comment inside the header), an /ObjStm no entry names, a row that does not land on its header, or pypdf finding nothing where a copy exists refuses the file. Round-4 repros (6 hostile, 3 heavy controls) refused; light twins decided by the identity check both ways. Owner chose strict (no incremental-update exception): 5 genuine fixtures (90, 174, 281, 531, 849; two-section incremental updates) are now refused by the layer gate and go to the Vision route. Census 870: refused 7 (305, 668 and those 5). Review round 1 (same day, version kept, unshipped): every cross-reference row in every section and generation is walked (pdf_xref_rows): types n or f only, an in-use row must sit on its number's one header, one generation in use per number, a packed lookup must match stream and index; every percent sign on a line is tried; object-stream owners by bisect; odd-word scans charged their real cost. Census 870: refused 9 (the 7, plus 191 and 246: one-section tables numbered from 1, each row one object off its header). Review round 2 (same day, version kept, unshipped): the walk reads the whole cross-reference chain or refuses the file (a start pdfium reads differently from pypdf, a link to where no section starts, a loop, a link that is not a whole number); /Prev 0 ends the chain, /XRefStm 0 is no link; pdfium's startxref search is copied byte for byte and checked by probe. Where pdfium finds no start (a tail longer than 4096 bytes) it rebuilds from the headers: the file passes on the one-header rule with pypdf's whole chain checked, and every /Root and /Encrypt in the raw file must name what pypdf's trailer names (probe: the rebuild takes the last trailer). Bytes before the header: pdfium's offsets count from its header. Census 870: refused 9, unchanged. Review round 3 (same day, version kept, unshipped): pdfium also reads bytes 0x80 and 0xff as white space; every finding scan (object headers, 'obj' words, /Root, /Encrypt and /ObjStm names, '#' names) now treats them, and 0x0b, as white space in every mode, so a header or name pdfium reads is always found; an accepting match (a cross-reference row, a reference) stays on the white space both readers share, so a header or reference that only one reader would read is refused. Each watched or '#' name is charged a word's work, and each escape more. Census 870: refused 9, unchanged.

2.3.5.note: OCR-20 (2026-11-24), the sticker gap: pdfium draws annotations over the page, while pypdf reads the text under them. Owner's strict rule: a page whose /Annots holds anything but a /Link with no /AP has no exact text layer (pdf_annots.annots_hide, first check in pdf_pages._page_visibility, so the text layer, page texts, first_page_drawn and the rules lane all lose it); /Annots on a /Parent, /Annots that is not an array, a non-dictionary entry or a missing or odd /Subtype also hide the page. The entries are charged to the per-document budget (MAX_DOC_ANNOTS 2,000, past it OVER_BUDGET). pdfium agrees: the worker's paint check and the ink check fail a page with any annotation but a /Link with no AP key. Census 870: refused 12, unchanged (the render gate does not read the layer). Wider compare (848): 8 files change layer, texts and rules (6 also layout): 6 with a /Link with /AP (blank q Q or empty pictures), 1 /Stamp with /AP, and 1 /FreeText with /AP the render gate already refuses; so 7 extra genuine files go to Vision. Max genuine reader 2.96 % of the work cap (unchanged). Review round 1 (2026-11-25, not shipped, so the digest was updated in place): a dictionary key named twice refuses the file in the gate (pypdf keeps the first value, pdfium the last; pdf_dict_keys); pdfium now judges every page pypdf judged, blank ones too; the SPM words op refuses a page whose own paint check fails. Census 870: refused 18 (6 more, each a key named twice). Review round 2 (2026-11-25, not shipped, digest updated in place): the gate also refuses the file when pypdf reads a dictionary, array or name leniently where pdfium reads on (a dictionary not ending on '>>' or not read as one key and one value per entry: a null key, a skipped non-name key, a partial read; an array not ending on its own ']'; null / true / false not standing whole; a name of 128 bytes or more, raw or decoded; any pypdf warning while a dictionary is read), checked structurally in pdf_dict_keys for the file, object streams and the content streams the page walk parses; pdfium's paint check and the SPM words op refuse a page drawing an XObject with /OC (pdfium_type3.page_flags, as the ink op). Census 870: refused 18 (same list). Wider compare (848): only the 6 round-1 files differ, in the gate's refusal text; 0 extra genuine files. Max genuine reader 2.96 % of the work cap (unchanged). See decisions.md 2026-11-25 round 2. Review round 3 part 1 (2026-11-25, not shipped, digest updated in place): content-stream bytes pypdf and pdfium tokenise differently hide the page (pdf_content_bytes, before each content stream is parsed): 0x80, 0xFF or 0x0B outside a string or comment; a word that is no PDF operator (also inside BX/EX); an octal escape over 255, a backslash before a byte outside pypdf's escape table, or before LF LF, LF CR or CR CR; a comment, string or hex string open where a /Contents array stream ends, or a later stream opening with '>'. An inline image's BI is found when 0x80 or 0xFF ends it. Census 870: refused 18 (same list). Wider compare (848): no file differs from round 2, so 0 extra genuine files (a first run found 3 genuine letters whose text holds ' BI)', a subject, so the inline-image search ends BI only on white space or a slash). Max genuine reader 2.96 % (unchanged) of the work cap. See decisions.md 2026-11-25 round 3 part 1. Round 3 part 2 (H4-H6): a wrong /Length or an odd 'stream' keyword refuses the file; null/true/false in an array must end at white space or a delimiter; /ActualText makes the SPM words op return no words. Census 870: refused 18 (same list); wider compare (848): 0 differ from part 1. See decisions.md 2026-11-25 round 3 part 2. Round 3 part 3 (H5, the short check; owner: tests only): a reference holding, or a number or reference ending on, a byte pypdf and pdfium disagree is white space (0x00, 0x0B, 0x80, 0xFF) refuses the file. Census 870: refused 18 (same list). Follow-up: in a content stream a NUL after a number is allowed (no references there; NUL is white space to both readers), since the wider compare found 20 genuine STPM files had lost their text layer.

2.3.6.note: TD-740 (2026-11-25): pdfium hides a page whose text object reaches past the page box it draws (the CropBox cut to the MediaBox) by more than 3 pt, or whose centre is off that box, judged in page space through every form's matrix (new pdfium_place.py; the paint check and the SPM words op). pypdf reads text wherever it is placed; pdfium draws only the page box. Refuse, not drop. Census 870: refused 18 (same list). Fixtures: 6 genuine files (3 shapes, 2 files each) lose their text layer (letters and digits placed 44 to 108 pt left of the page); 6 more with a line 1.9 pt past the right edge read as before. See decisions.md 25 Nov, TD-740. Review round 1 (2026-11-25, not shipped, digest updated in place): a Type3 box is its glyph's d1 box, which can lie, so every Type3 code shown on a page must keep its ink inside its d1 box and paint, unless pypdf reads it as blank (pdfium_type3.shown_ok, in the paint check); otherwise the page is hidden. 0 of 54 Type3 fixture files change. Review round 2 (2026-11-25, not shipped, digest updated in place): a Type3 glyph must really ink, measured by pdfium on a glyph sheet rendered at two scales (pdfium_type3.glyph_ink; a hairline, an empty path, a cancelled fill or a speck is no ink), and a glyph that inks nothing may only show a whitespace byte every candidate font reads as blank; a form with /Parent and no /Resources, or a /Pages node font name that clashes with the page, hides the page; a form drawn again under other resources is judged again. Review round 3 (2026-11-25, not shipped, digest updated in place): a Type3 code whose glyph inks nothing passes only when pdfium's own text page reads it as whitespace or nothing (pdfium_type3.pdfium_blank: each code shown alone at 1000 pt on a text sheet, read in the child by pdfium_place.sheet_text) and pypdf reads it as whitespace; our own /ToUnicode reader now only refuses. Every dictionary value the TD-740 walks compare or follow is resolved first (pdfium_type3._val: a /Subtype, /Resources, /Font, /CharProcs, /Encoding, /Differences, /FontMatrix item or /PatternType given by reference).
